problem:
Harbour Energy's customer service team receives three kinds of money-back request and treats them as the same thing: a return, a refund and a reversal. They are not the same, and confusing them costs the company money. A return is initiated by the debtor PSP, usually because the account cannot be debited, for example because the account is closed or the funds are insufficient, and it is carried by pacs.004. A refund is initiated by the debtor, who asks their bank to give the money back for an authorised collection under the scheme refund right. A reversal is initiated by the creditor, who has discovered an error after settlement and asks for the collection to be undone. Each has a different initiating party, a different message, different timing rules and different ledger treatment.

The timing rules are where the confusion is most expensive. For SDD Core, an authorised collection can be refunded on a no-questions-asked basis within 8 weeks of the debit date, and an unauthorised collection can be claimed within 13 months. SDD B2B has no authorised refund right at all, so a B2B debtor who asks for an authorised refund must be told that the right does not exist and given the correct alternative. The return windows differ too: B2B returns within D+3 Inter-PSP Business Days against Core D+5. A reversal is only possible from the settlement date and within 5 Inter-PSP Business Days following the due date. A team that applies the Core refund window to a B2B collection, or that treats a reversal as a refund, will pay money it did not need to pay or miss a deadline it should have met.

Harbour Energy needs a decision framework that asks, for every money-back case: who initiated it, which scheme applies, when was the debit, was the collection authorised, and which mechanism is available. Only then can the team give the customer the right answer and post the right ledger entry.
solution:
Start with a classification table that the customer service team can use on every case. The first question is who initiated it: the debtor PSP means a return, the debtor means a refund, the creditor means a reversal. The second question is the scheme: SDD Core or SDD B2B. The third is authorisation: was the collection authorised or not. The fourth is timing: the debit date for a refund, the due date for a reversal, and the return date for a return. With those four answers, the applicable mechanism and its window follow from the rules, and the team can give the customer a correct answer instead of a guess.

Teach the windows as a table and keep it current against the rulebook. For SDD Core, an authorised refund is available no-questions-asked within 8 weeks of the debit date, and an unauthorised claim within 13 months. SDD B2B has no authorised refund right. Returns are within D+3 Inter-PSP Business Days for B2B and D+5 for Core. A reversal is only possible from the settlement date and within 5 Inter-PSP Business Days following the due date. The pacs.004 message is the SDD return message used for both returns and refunds, so the team must not assume that a pacs.004 always means the same kind of event.

Finally, enforce the ledger discipline. Every money-back event is a separate linked transaction against the original collection, with the original instruction reference preserved, and the original collection is never deleted or altered. Keep separate worklists for returns, refunds and reversals, because each has its own deadlines and evidence needs, and reconcile each population separately. Report monthly on how many cases were classified correctly at first contact, how many were refused for the wrong reason, and how many missed a deadline, so the framework can be improved where it fails.

decision.question: You are the business analyst for Harbour Energy. A debtor asks for a refund of an authorised SDD B2B collection, a debtor PSP returns a Core collection for a closed account, and the billing team wants to reverse a settled collection a month after the due date. Customer service treats all three as the same kind of request. What framework do you recommend?

options.label: A
options.detail: Refuse every money-back request to protect revenue.

options.label: B
options.detail: Delete the original collection from the ledger and re-collect the correct amount.

options.label: C
options.detail: Classify the case by initiating party and scheme, check authorisation and the applicable window, and process the valid mechanism as a separate linked event with the original collection intact.

options.label: D
options.detail: Treat all three as refunds and pay every request within 13 months.

decisionRationale: Option C is correct because it distinguishes the three mechanisms by initiating party and scheme, applies the correct window to each, and preserves the original collection as a financial record. Option D pays refunds that do not exist, since B2B has no authorised refund right, and ignores the different windows. Option A refuses valid claims. Option B deletes a financial record, which destroys the audit trail.

steps.title: Raises a money-back request, or identifies an error after settlement
Identifies the mechanism: return, refund or reversal, based on who initiated it and the scheme
Validates the scheme, the collection date, authorisation status and the applicable deadline
Checks the window: 8 weeks for an authorised Core refund, 13 months for an unauthorised claim, D+3 or D+5 for returns, 5 Inter-PSP Business Days after the due date for a reversal
Rejects the request with the correct explanation if the window has passed or the right does not exist
Processes the valid return, refund or reversal as a separate linked event against the original collection
Posts the linked accounting entries without altering the original collection
Reconciles the money-back event against the original collection and the clearing report

happy: A money-back case is classified correctly by initiating party and scheme, the applicable window is checked against the debit or due date, and the valid mechanism is processed as a separate linked event with the original collection intact. The customer receives a clear outcome, and the ledger reconciles. A case that is out of time or has no right is refused with the correct explanation and the alternative offered.

negative.title: Authorised refund requested on a B2B collection
negative.detail: A debtor asks for a refund of an authorised SDD B2B collection. Apply the correct rule for that scheme. For B2B, explain that no authorised refund right exists and offer the correct alternative, such as contacting the creditor.

negative.title: Request outside the applicable window
negative.detail: A refund or reversal is requested after its deadline has passed. Refuse the request with the correct explanation, record the decision, and offer the alternative that applies, for example a commercial goodwill gesture or a dispute with the creditor.

negative.title: Authorisation disputed
negative.detail: The debtor says the collection was never authorised. Treat the claim as unauthorised, apply the 13-month window, investigate the authorisation evidence, and do not apply the 8-week authorised window to it.

negative.title: Return for a closed account
negative.detail: A return arrives after the original customer account has been closed. Apply the closed-account policy, route the funds to the approved suspense or unclaimed-funds process, and keep the funds traceable to the original collection.

negative.title: Duplicate reversal
negative.detail: The same reversal is submitted twice for one original collection. Reject the duplicate, link it to the first reversal, and reconcile to a single posting.

technical: Model each money-back event as a separate linked transaction with its own type, return, refund or reversal, its initiating party, its scheme, its window and its deadline, all linked to the original collection by instruction reference. Store the debit date, the due date and the settlement date on the original collection, because each window is counted from a different one. Enforce the window rules in the claims service with effective-dated rule configuration, and never let a window be applied from the wrong scheme. Use pacs.004 for SDD returns and refunds, and camt.056 with camt.029 where a cancellation is the applicable mechanism, keeping the cancellation request separate from the original payment. Retain the classification decision, the evidence and the customer explanation in the audit record.

messages.title: Payment return carrying a return or a refund-related return between PSPs, used for both returns and refunds in SDD

fields.tag: Original instruction identification and return reason code
fields.name: Original instruction identification and return reason code

messages.title: Payment status report for the outcome of the original collection and of the money-back event
Cancellation request where a cancellation, rather than a return or refund, is the applicable mechanism, paired with camt.029
Resolution of an investigation, confirming whether a camt.056 cancellation request was accepted or rejected

accounting: A return debits the creditor and credits the debtor's bank for the returned amount, a refund credits the debtor and is recovered from the creditor, and a reversal debits the creditor and credits the debtor, each as a separate linked event against the original collection. The original collection is never deleted or altered. Operations works from separate worklists for returns, refunds and reversals, because each has its own deadlines and evidence requirements, and Finance reconciles each population separately against the clearing and ledger reports. A refund paid outside its window, or a reversal submitted after its deadline, is rejected and escalated rather than posted silently.

scenarios.given: an eligible authorised Core collection refund request within 8 weeks of the debit date
scenarios.then: the bank applies the scheme-defined refund process

scenarios.given: an authorised B2B collection refund request
scenarios.then: it is refused because SDD B2B has no authorised refund right, and the customer is told the correct alternative

scenarios.given: a settled collection eligible for reversal within 5 Inter-PSP Business Days following the due date
scenarios.then: the reversal is linked to the original and posted once

scenarios.given: a return received for a closed account
scenarios.then: the closed-account policy is applied and funds remain traceable

Refuse it, explaining that SDD B2B has no authorised refund right, and offer the correct alternative

options: D+3 for B2B against D+5 for Core
